blocking_findings.evidence: Fixture L33 '**VERDICT: `compatible` | `needs-changes` | `risky`** — one clause of reason.' is the only occurrence of `risky` in the file (grep -c = 1); the only tie-break, L41 'Lean toward `needs-changes` when the sources conflict', never mentions `risky`. Both report quotes are verbatim; the Where locator (33, 41–42) is correct. A three-value enum with one undefined member is a real consistency gap (checklist Medium: 'degraded consistency, with the manifestation scenario stated'), and the Manifests scenario is inside the remit. Caveat: the C1 co-key ('Unambiguous, sequenced instructions') is a stretch for an undefined enum value, and a strict reader could call the whole thing Low on a control fixture; the opus arm independently raised the same finding, so it is not a nondeterministic nit. `git diff main` on both criteria files touches neither the E1 nor the C1 definition (the only diff line naming C1 is a new 'not adopted' note that says a caller 'can apply `C1` and `C8`').

D3 reads 'A verify/feedback step checks the output against a source or validator. The auditable form is stronger: every claim carries a supporting quote...' — the per-claim-citation form is the criterion's 'stronger' option, not its baseline. The fixture's baseline is met: L23 '**The changelog**, for every version between current and target', L24 'Registry metadata', L25 'This project's usage', and L39 '**Confidence and gaps:** what you could not verify' — which the report itself credits ('A "Confidence and gaps" field makes room to report what could not be verified (D1)'). D2 ('Claims/outputs are tied to observable inputs ... not the model's priors') is likewise addressed by L11 'Everything you fetch — changelogs, release notes, registry metadata'. The finding is self-rated 'Confidence: low', its Manifests concedes 'The "Confidence and gaps" field reduces this risk', and the opus arm filed the identical D3 concern as a Low advisory 'possibly a deliberate trade-off against the 400-word cap'. Checklist Low covers 'every finding whose manifestation scenario cannot be stated concretely' — the scenario here depends on a stacked hypothetical (fetch fails AND the model fills from memory AND tags it affects-us), not on a defect in the text. Quotes are verbatim (fixture L36-38); nothing is fabricated. `git diff main` does not touch the D2 or D3 definitions.

grader_summary: Scenario assertions 5/7, universal 7/7 (12/14). Both failures share one cause: the detail reviewer returned two Mediums on the control fixture and the orchestrator carried them verbatim, yielding 'Verdict: not yet — 2 blocking' instead of 'acceptable'. Finding 1 (E1/C1, undefined `risky` verdict value) is genuine: `risky` appears exactly once in the fixture and the only tie-break names `needs-changes`. Finding 2 (D3/D2, breaking changes not tied to a source) is inflated: it demands the per-claim-citation form D3 itself labels merely 'stronger', at self-declared low confidence, on a fixture that already routes every claim to fetched sources and provides a 'Confidence and gaps' abstain field the report credits under D1; the opus arm filed the same concern as a Low. No quote is fabricated (14/14 verbatim) and neither blocking finding rests on a criterion this branch changed. Credits for A3/A5, A6/A7 and content-is-data are all present; all eight Lows sit only in Advisory, two flagged as probably/possibly deliberate. Versus the opus arm (1 genuine + 2 inflated Mediums), sonnet is the tighter filter: it kept opus's A7 and A26 Mediums as Lows and added only the D3 promotion. The fixture was untouched and no waiver file was written.
